'''Germán Saúl Sánchez Sánchez''' (born 24 June 1992) is a Mexican diver.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://secure.meetcontrol.com/divemeets/system/profile.php?number=23694 |title=Diver Profile: German Sanchez |publisher=divemeets.com |accessdate=21 April 2012}}</ref> He is nicknamed "Duva". At the age of 16, he competed in the Men's individual 10m platform at the [[2008 Summer Olympics]] and came in 22nd.<ref>{{Cite web|title = 10m platform men results - Diving - Beijing 2008 Olympics|url = http://www.olympic.org/olympic-results/beijing-2008/diving/10m-platform-m|website = olympic.org|accessdate = 2015-05-03}}</ref> He won one gold medal in the 2011 [[Pan-American Games]]. At the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in London, he won a silver medal in the synchronized 10m platform with his partner [[Iván García (diver)|Iván García]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.olympic.org/olympic-results/london-2012/diving/synchronized-diving-10m-platform-m?games=&sport=31800&event=31808|title = LONDON 2012 DIVING,SYNCHRONIZED DIVING 10M PLATFORM MEN-FINAL|date =30 July 2012 |website = Official website of the Olympic Movement}}</ref> In the individual 10m platform, Sánchez came 14th.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.olympic.org/olympic-results/london-2012/diving/10m-platform-m|title = LONDON 2012 DIVING,10M PLATFORM MEN-FINAL|date =12 August 2012 |website = Official website of the Olympic Movement}}</ref> In 2016, Sánchez took part in his third Olympic Games in [[Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]], where he came 5th in the synchronized 10m platform, again alongside [[Iván García (diver)|Iván García]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/D/V/DVM210101_DetailedResults_2016_08_08_75782ff1_b173_4eff_83d8_5a5fa28539ef.pdf|title=Results-Men's Synchronised 10m Platform Final|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920020031/https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/D/V/DVM210101_DetailedResults_2016_08_08_75782ff1_b173_4eff_83d8_5a5fa28539ef.pdf|archive-date=20 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Twelve days later, Sánchez won the silver medal in individual 10m platform.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/D/V/DVM010901_DetailedResults_2016_08_19_0d7cf265_1f3c_4751_abc4_f676d77b2bf8.pdf|title=Results-Men's 10m Platform Preliminary|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920194530/https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/D/V/DVM010901_DetailedResults_2016_08_19_0d7cf265_1f3c_4751_abc4_f676d77b2bf8.pdf|archive-date=20 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and 9th in the semi-final.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/D/V/DVM010201_DetailedResults_2016_08_20_d5570064_9803_4a00_8ef6_c4cc4a5b8be7.pdf|title=Results-Men's 10m Platform Semi-Final|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920194410/https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/D/V/DVM010201_DetailedResults_2016_08_20_d5570064_9803_4a00_8ef6_c4cc4a5b8be7.pdf|archive-date=20 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/D/V/DVM010101_DetailedResults_2016_08_20_84406123_a24c_406e_a1fc_0b8bea4c55d0.pdf|title=Results-Men's 10m Platform Final|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920193242/https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/D/V/DVM010101_DetailedResults_2016_08_20_84406123_a24c_406e_a1fc_0b8bea4c55d0.pdf|archive-date=20 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He became the third Mexican athlete to win an Olympic silver medal in Men's individual 10m platform after [[Joaquín Capilla]] (1952) and [[Álvaro Gaxiola]] (1968). He was the only Mexican diver who had won Olympic medals in both individual and synchronized events until Osmar Olvera did it in Paris 2024.

==Technical features== 
Sánchez is a talented diver who has mastered a series of the most difficult dives since 2012. The dives which he uses now in the competition and their degrees of difficulty are: Forward 4½ Somersaults-Tuck 109C (3.7), Back 3½ Somersaults-Tuck 207C (3.3), Reverse 3½ Somersaults-Tuck 307C (3.4), Inward 4½ Somersaults-Tuck 409C (4.1), Forward 2½ Somersaults 3 Twists-Pike 5156B (3.8) and Armstand Back 3 Somersaults-Tuck 626C (3.3).<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.omegatiming.com/File/Download?id=00010F0003010302FFFFFFFFFFFFFF01|website = omegatiming.com|accessdate = 2015-05-03}}</ref> The total degree of difficulty of his dives is 21.6, which is the world's third greatest following Iván García(MEX) and Yang Jian(CHN).{{Citation needed|date=March 2019}} Of his dives, 409C is the most difficult.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/rules/2015/disciplines/FINAdvrules_20152017.pdf |title=DIVING RULES |date=17 February 2015 |website=Official website of FINA |publisher=FINA |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402100418/http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/rules/2015/disciplines/FINAdvrules_20152017.pdf |archivedate= 2 April 2015 }}</ref> However, due to the high level of difficulty, he cannot perform the dives perfectly all the time. It is common for him to perform unsteadily.{{Citation needed|date=March 2019}}

==Olympic experiences== 
Sánchez took part in his first Olympic Games at the [[2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Beijing Olympic Games]] at the age of 16. He only participated in the individual 10m platform. The six dives he performed were respectively 5253B, 207C, 307C, 6142D, 407C, and 109C. The total degree of difficulty was only 19.9, which was not enough to be competitive. As a result, he was eliminated after the qualifying round with a score of 399.35 and a final ranking of 22nd.<ref name="sports-reference.com">{{Cite web|title=Germán Sánchez Bio, Stats, and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/sa/german-sanchez-3.html |website=Olympics at Sports-Reference.com |accessdate=2015-06-02 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150530115746/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/sa/german-sanchez-3.html |archivedate=30 May 2015 }}</ref>

Sánchez qualified to participate in both the individual and synchronized 10m platform at the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] with his performance at the [[2012 FINA Diving World Cup]] where he achieved the silver medal alongside [[Iván García (diver)|Iván García]]. This time, the dives he performed were much more competitive than those of 2008 Beijing Olympic Games. The six dives they performed in the synchronized 10m platform were 401B, 201B, 109C, 409C, 307C, 5156B. They performed all of their dives almost perfectly, coming in second with a score of 468.90, 17.88 points behind Chinese divers [[Cao Yuan]] and [[Zhang Yanquan]].<ref name="sports-reference.com"/>

In the individual event, the six dives Sánchez performed were 207C, 5156B, 626C, 409C, 307C, 109C. The total degree of difficulty was 21.5, however due to a poor performance in the dive 626C, he was eliminated after the semi-final, ranked 14th.<ref name="sports-reference.com"/>

At the age of 24, Sánchez participated in his third Olympic Games - [[2016 Summer Olympics]]. He was qualified to participate in both individual and synchronized 10m platform with [[Iván García (diver)|Iván García]]. In the synchronized 10m platform, their dives were different from those at [[2012 Summer Olympics]]. Their six dives were 401B, 301B, 5255B, 109C, 207C, and 5156B.  Without 409C, their total difficult degrees were 18.4, which was still the highest in that competition. They ended up in 5th place, after [[Chen Aisen]]/[[Lin Yue]] (CHN), [[David Boudia]]/[[Steele Johnson]] (USA), [[Tom Daley|Thomas Daley]]/[[Daniel Goodfellow]] (GBR), and [[Patrick Hausding]]/[[Sascha Klein]] (GER).

Twelve days later, Sánchez dived in the final of the individual 10m platform, after ranking only 12th in the preliminary<ref name=":0" /> and 9th in the semi-final.<ref name=":1" /> Due to injury, he adjusted his dives and the overall degree of difficulty was reduced to 20.7. In contrast to his sub-par performances in the preliminary and semi-final rounds, he performed every dive steadily and won the silver medal with a high score of 532.70.<ref name=":2" />

==Competitive history==
Sánchez became a professional diver at the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing. From then on, he has been representing [[Mexico]] FINA World Junior Diving Championships,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fina.org/H2O/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=3156:aachen-2008-boys-10m&catid=362:results-archives&Itemid=1376 |title=Aachen 2008 - Boys 10M RESULTS (ARCHIVES) |date=15 October 2012 |website=Official website of FINA |publisher=FINA |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402114923/http://www.fina.org/H2O/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=3156%3Aaachen-2008-boys-10m&catid=362%3Aresults-archives&Itemid=1376 |archivedate= 2 April 2015 }}</ref> [[FINA World Aquatics Championships]], [[Olympic Games]], [[FINA Diving World Cup]], [[FINA Diving World Series]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/histofina/diving.pdf |title=HistoFINA-DIVING MEDALLISTS AND STATISTICS |date=31 January 2015 |website=Official website of FINA |publisher=FINA |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402105138/http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/histofina/diving.pdf |archivedate= 2 April 2015 }}</ref> [[Pan American Games]] and [[Central American and Caribbean Games]]. He has won many medals from these competitions since 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/histofina/diving.pdf |title=HistoFINA-DIVING MEDALLISTS AND STATISTICS |date=31 January 2015 |website=Official website of FINA |publisher=FINA |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402105138/http://www.fina.org/H2O/docs/histofina/diving.pdf |archivedate= 2 April 2015 }}</ref> He has won one gold medal in the [[Diving at the 2011 Pan American Games|Pan American Games in 2011]], as well as Olympic silver medals in London 2012 (synchronized) and Rio 2016 (individual).<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://sportspedia.com.mx/en-vivo-final-10-metros-plataforma-varonil-mexico-busca-medalla/|title = ¡México es plata en clavados!|date = 20 August 2016|accessdate = 21 August 2016|website = Sportspedia México|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160918050839/http://sportspedia.com.mx/en-vivo-final-10-metros-plataforma-varonil-mexico-busca-medalla/|archive-date = 18 September 2016|url-status = dead}}</ref>
